method.multiples: Trailing twelve months. EV = month-end price x basic shares outstanding + debt - cash and marketable securities (short and long term).
method.adj_ebitda: Operating income + D&A + stock-based compensation; EV/adjusted EBITDA shown only where the adjusted margin is 10% or more.
method.rev_growth: Trailing twelve months of revenue against the same period a year earlier, as reported (includes acquisitions).
method.aggregate: Median of members. A company leaves the index in the month its acquisition is announced, because its share price then reflects the offer; the deal is shown at the price paid, marked pending until it closes.
method.shares: Basic shares outstanding; figures are slightly understated against fully diluted counts.
method.deals: Deal price per share x basic shares, using the last quarter ended at least 30 days before announcement. Deal enterprise value (ev_m, $ millions) is on the same basis, so it can be below the headline value, which usually counts all options and awards.
method.rule_of_40: Each current member is placed by revenue growth plus margin (Rule of 40 threshold: 40 percentage points) and by EV/revenue against the index median, giving four quadrants. Margin is adjusted EBITDA margin by default; the chart can also show margin after stock-based compensation. A fitted line is computed for reference only (rule_of_40_fit) and is not shown, because it explains little of the spread in most indexes.
method.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL filings; month-end market prices.

notes: Small deal: target revenue under $50 million.
